trust_decision.summary: A wire-format length prefix read from untrusted bytes is trusted to be within the enclosing message before it is added to the cursor/pointer or handed to a preallocator. The decision is made per consumer (checkedLimit/remainingInLimit in the Kotlin readers, endPointer in the Swift ReadBuffer), not at the varint producer, and each of the three independent decoder implementations had to make it separately: ByteArrayProtoReader32 (Int cursor), ProtoReader (Long cursor) and the Swift runtime.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names ByteArrayProtoReader32, and `limit = pos + length` is the 32-bit cursor overflow: with length = Int.MAX_VALUE the sum wraps negative, so the very next line's `if (limit > pushedLimit)` cannot catch it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and its title name ByteArrayProtoReader32 only, and ProtoReader is a different class whose `limit = pos + length` is Long arithmetic already followed by `if (limit > pushedLimit)`, so it reads as a reader that cannot overflow.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Packed repeated fields legitimately preallocate from the announced length (`forDecoding(reader.nextFieldMinLengthInBytes(), n)`), and a valid field whose length exactly fills the remaining bytes must still decode; an over-broad fix that caps the length, or uses `>=` instead of `>` in the remaining-bytes test, breaks both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the Int overload of forDecoding builds IntArray(rawLength / minSize) with no coerceAtMost and no negative guard, while its Long sibling at IntArrayList.kt:46-54 clamps; the same gap exists in FloatArrayList/LongArrayList/DoubleArrayList
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the generated packed-field decoders call this on every first occurrence of a packed field (wire-golden-files/src/main/kotlin/squareup/wire/alltypes/AllTypes.kt:4153), and the Swift fix explicitly names this preallocation path, so a maintainer adding a fourth runtime or an Int-cursor fast path would plausibly copy the unclamped overload

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third delegating reader that re-implements nextLengthDelimited / nextFieldMinLengthInBytes as direct Int->Long conversions without any limit test of its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file's own comment says ProtoReader was not designed to be subclassed this way and warns every method must be mirrored; a maintainer adding a cached limit or an offset in the wrapper is a natural place for a sibling miss

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 4-byte big-endian frame length read from the wire and used to bound a Buffer without a max-size check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: gRPC length-prefixed framing sits directly on top of the decoder and a maintainer hardening 'unauthenticated length' would plausibly add the same check here as a separate commit

O9_family: integer overflow / wrapping length arithmetic (CWE-190) used unchecked for cursor and allocation math

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle wrapper with the kotlin-multiplatform plugin for wire-runtime; a separate Swift toolchain plus Xcode for wire-runtime-swift (build.gradle.kts links Mach-O bundles and adds -F $DEVELOPER_DIR/Developer/Library/Frameworks, so the Swift tests are macOS/Xcode only)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add a negative/Int.MAX_VALUE length guard in ByteArrayProtoReader32.nextLengthDelimited (the class the report names) and stop there, leaving the Long-cursor ProtoReader and the preallocation path untouched

out_of_scope_notes: Out of scope and not pursued: the same class of unchecked wire length also appears outside the protobuf decoder in gRPC framing (wire-grpc-client/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/squareup/wire/internal/GrpcMessageSource.kt:55); it is only noted as injection room, not as a route of this advisory.
